citation.title: Data augmentation for disruption prediction via robust surrogate models
citation.authors: Rath, K.; Rügamer, D.; Bischl, B.; von Toussaint, U.; Rea, C.; Maris, A.; Granetz, R.; Albert, C. G.

topic: Augmenting DIII-D disruption time-series training data with a state-space Student-t process surrogate, followed by post-hoc colouring transformations.
own_question: Can a small set of discharges (3 to 6 shots per class) be used to generate statistically similar multivariate time series of five global signals (βn, li, κ, q95, n/nG)?
actual_method_and_evidence: A per-signal uncorrelated Student-t filter and smoother with a Matérn 3/2 kernel. Correlations are imposed afterwards by colouring. Three DIII-D 2016 disruption classes were sampled at 25 ms. The generated data were checked against the training data using Wasserstein distance, MMD, PSD, DTW, mfPCA and SOM. No downstream predictor improvement was demonstrated, and none of this involves nowcasting, CES, BES or ECEI.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline smoothing over whole discharges, so it is two-sided rather than causal. Arrival times are not addressed.
validation_if_relevant: Similarity metrics computed against the same training shots. There is no held-out test.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as evidence of a causal or online estimator.
Do not cite it as evidence that a Student-t or GP model improves disruption prediction.
Do not treat it as CES, ion-temperature or pedestal work.
Do not conclude that state-space TP achieves 10 ms real-time computation in our setting.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude by default. The paper concerns offline data augmentation, not nowcasting. At most, it could support a single theory-background sentence: Solin–Särkkä state-space TP filtering scales O(N) and is robust to outliers. Citing the primary sources for that point is preferable.
